Member when many hardware and even drug stores had tube testers?

My hometown was very small but we did have a Radio Shack. Up through the early 80s they still had a tube tester in the store. I remember thinking how out of date it was since the store was selling TRS-80 computers by then and the tube tester seemed so anachronistic. I miss the old Radio Shack days. It's weird not having them around anymore.
Back in those days RS was the only place you could count on to buy components like resistors, capacitors, transistors, etc. How times change.

Throughout the late 70s and 80s I would anxiously await each year's Radio Shack catalog release. The new components they would stock that year were sources of new project inspiration for me. Some of the most notable parts were had in the 80s when Archer had amazing new things like the General Instruments talking clock chip (SP-0256-017), the GI speech chip and controller (SP-0256-AL2 and SP-0256-CTS), the touch tone decoder IC and the analog message recording IC. I built projects around all of these parts, though some were more successful than the others. It was a wonderful time to be an electronics hobbyist. Sadly the 90s and the SMT revolution shut down my ability to work with all the new components of the 90s and early 2000s but the world of the hobbyist/maker is strong today. I just wish making still had the same wonder as it did back then but it is nice to have so much available now.
